## The editor's top-level WORKSPACES are a tab strip at the window top bar's left, and the Autotile Rules workspace edits rule sets LIVE through the ONE shared history

The editor has **top-level workspaces** (WS — the Blender workspace-tab model): `EditorWorkspace` is
`LevelEditor` (the familiar shell — viewport + panels + shelf) or `AutotileRules` (a full-window rule-set
editor with its own pane disposition: rule-set list, the 16 exposure cases, the tileset sheet), held as
`EditorShellStateComponent.ActiveWorkspace` — session state, never serialized. `WorkspaceTabStripSystem`
renders and hit-tests the two tabs at the window **top bar's LEFT** in the one tab language the panel and
viewport strips already speak (active = `Bg1` fill + `Accent` underline; inactive = `Bg0` hover-fading to
`Bg2`), which is why `EditorChromeBuilder.DefaultButtons` — now exactly **Undo / Redo / Refresh** — is
laid **right-anchored** by `EditorChromeLayout.TopBarRightRow`: the bar's two clusters own opposite ends
and cannot collide. The strip is live in **both** transport states, stands down while a shell
splitter/scrollbar drag owns the pointer, and never writes `ActiveWorkspace` itself — a click dispatches
into the composer-supplied switch.

**One switch owner.** `EditorOverlay.SetActiveWorkspace` is that owner (the tab click AND the
`workspace:level-editor|autotile-rules` ops), and it is where entering a workspace MEANS something:
entering `AutotileRules` is an EDITING view, so it is **refused loudly while Playing** ("Pause to edit
autotile rules" — the same refusal `OpenLayerRulesEditor` applies to the layer menu's "Edit Autotile
Rules…" jump), and leaving lands back on the Level Editor shell.
`AutotileRuleEditorSystem.IsOpen` **derives** from `ActiveWorkspace` — there is no second open flag to
desync — and while it is open the workspace owns the pointer BELOW the top bar (it swallows the cursor
edges so nothing beneath re-picks or places, leaving the tabs and Undo/Redo live above) and ORs into the
editor keyboard's suppression, exactly like a dialog. **A switch is not an edit:** selection, the ONE
shared `EditorHistory` (its count and its `EditVersion`), the ACTIVE layer, and the rules view's own
binding (layer, rule set, selected case) all survive the round trip — only the presented panes change.

**Edits are LIVE and undoable — there is no Save/Cancel.** Every rules-workspace mutation (a case's tile
toggle, a tileset pick) is one `PaintValueEditCommand` pushed through that same shared history, keyed by
the value's stable `TilePaintValue.Id` — indices shift when values are added or removed, ids never do.
`Apply`/`Revert` write `AutotileRules` / `TilesetKey` / `TileSize` and publish
`NotifyChanged<TileGridComponent>`, which IS the debounced bake's trigger, so the painted world re-skins
within the bake's quiet window and Ctrl+Z walks a rules edit back like any other scene edit. A rules edit
keeps the tileset and a tileset re-bind keeps the rules (masks are sheet-agnostic; the cell indices are
the designer's to fix up next), and a case can never be emptied — removing its last assignment restores
sheet cell 0,0, which is what `TileGridBaking.PickTile` assumes. Creating a rule set is the SAME
`AddPaintValueCommand` the paint shelf's `+ New` card fires (a rule set IS a paintable index), so the
workspace adds **no parallel data model**: everything it authors is `core.TileGrid` component state that
round-trips byte-stably. The view **heals its binding** every frame — a dead layer or an undone value
re-binds to the first surviving rule set — because undo/redo and deletes can invalidate the selection
under an open workspace.

**Why:** rules authoring needs three panes at once (rule sets, the 16 exposure cases, the sheet); that is
a workspace, not a floating modal over the shell, and Blender's answer to "a different task wants a
different whole-window layout" is a workspace tab. Making the edits live commands rather than a
Save/Cancel buffer is the call the rest of the editor already made — the history IS the safety net (the
one-data-model tenet) — and the designer watches the terrain re-skin while they toggle instead of after
they commit. Refusing entry while Playing keeps the editing-tools-are-inert-while-Playing contract
intact, and deriving `IsOpen` from `ActiveWorkspace` keeps a second, desyncable "is the rules view open"
flag from ever being born.
**Breaks:** a Save/Cancel buffer over the same values re-introduces exactly the parallel representation
the camera block cost three days of bugs; an edit that forgets `NotifyChanged` leaves the world showing
the OLD art until some unrelated change happens to re-bake (the designer concludes the rule "did
nothing"); a workspace that owns the pointer over the top bar traps the designer inside it (no tab, no
Undo); a switch that resets selection / history / active layer makes leaving the rules view cost the
session; entering the workspace while Playing means live edits fight the running simulation and a Ctrl+Z
races physics; keying the command by list INDEX instead of `Id` makes an undo after an add/remove rewrite
the WRONG rule set; letting a case go empty makes `PickTile` index an empty alternates array mid-bake; a
second `IsOpen` flag beside `ActiveWorkspace` desyncs the tab strip from the view it names.
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/WorkspaceTests.cs`
(`WorkspaceTabs_AreTwoAdjacentTabsAtTheTopBarsLeft_TheActiveOneUnderlined`,
`REDACTED` — the top bar's two clusters;
`ClickingTheInactiveWorkspaceTab_DispatchesTheSwitch_AndTheActiveTabIsInert`,
`WorkspaceTabs_SuppressedDuringAShellDrag_DispatchNothing` — the dispatch and its guards;
`REDACTED` — the refusal, and
that pausing lets the same click through;
`WorkspaceRoundTrip_PreservesSelection_History_ActiveLayer_AndTheBoundRuleSet` — the editing state
survives a switch (the selected CASE observed through the next toggle still landing on it);
`REDACTED` — the view parks and exactly
one tab is underlined);
`MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/AutotileRuleEditorTests.cs`
(`RulesEdit_ReBakesTheTileSourceRects_PerNeighborMask_AndUndoRestoresThem` — a rules edit through the
history changes the BAKED tile's source rect for the edited mask only, and undo/redo walk it back and
forth; `ToggleTile_ThroughTheWorkspace_IsOneUndoableStep_ThatReSkinsTheSelectedCase`,
`ToggleTile_NeverEmptiesACase_TheLastRemovalFallsBackToSheetCellZero`,
`ApplyTilesetPick_IsOneUndoableCommand_ThatKeepsTheRules`,
`SelectValueByName_BindsAcrossEveryGrid_AndIsCaseInsensitive`,
`UndoingARuleSetsCreation_ReBindsTheViewToASurvivingRuleSet` — the workspace verbs and the self-heal;
`SerializeRules_IsTheCanonicalDsl_ParseRulesReadsItBackUnchanged`;
`CreatedAndEditedRuleSet_RoundTripsThroughTheCanonicalSerializer` and
`RuleSetEdits_AreByteStable_LoadSaveIsAFixedPoint` — create → bind → author → save → load, with each
undo step round-tripping through the FILE too);
`MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/EditorContextMenuTests.cs`
(`EntityMenu_EditAutotileRules_AppearsExactlyForAPaintLayerSelection`,
`REDACTED` — the layer-menu jump).
The workspace's own DRAW (the three panes, the 3×3 case glyphs, the sheet thumbnails) has no test — it is
verified on the demo host like the other chrome draws; and the refusal-while-Playing POLICY is exercised
through a mirror of `EditorOverlay.SetActiveWorkspace` (the `MenuOver` precedent), because the overlay
itself is not unit-constructible.
**Depends on:** this file — "The Paint tab arms a tile-grid brush; the paint VIEW shows logical colored
blocks; strokes are one undo step" (the rule sets ARE that tab's paintable indices, and `+ New Rule Set…`
is its `+ New` card), "Bounded undo with drag-coalescing" (the ONE shared history every rules edit rides),
"Editor context menus are a data-driven popup: one model, two anchors, modal like the dialog" (the layer
menu's "Edit Autotile Rules…" jump and the tileset picker's filtered popup), "The editor toolbar's buttons
drive the same shared editor instances; the chrome is native-resolution on the Editor target, always on
while the editor is composed" (the top bar the tab strip shares with the right-anchored general buttons),
"The editor shell's region sizes, tabs, and drag ownership live in one shell-state component"
(`ActiveWorkspace`'s home + the drag token the strip honors), "Every level-editor color and depth is an
`EditorTheme` role" (the tab visuals and the workspace's depth band), "The transport's Restart rebuilds
the scene from the original load request and discards unsaved edits" (the
`EditorInfrastructureComponent` tag that keeps the workspace chrome alive across a Restart);
level-loading — "The paint grid is authored cells + values; everything visible/collidable is a bake
product" (what a rules edit re-derives, and the `core.TileGrid` round-trip the rule sets persist through).

editor keyboard's suppression, exactly like a dialog. **A switch is not an edit:** selection, the ONE
shared `EditorHistory` (its count and its `EditVersion`), the ACTIVE layer, and the rules view's own
binding (layer, rule set, selected case) all survive the round trip — only the presented panes change.

**Edits are LIVE and undoable — there is no Save/Cancel.** Every rules-workspace mutation (a case's tile
toggle, a tileset pick) is one `PaintValueEditCommand` pushed through that same shared history, keyed by
the value's stable `TilePaintValue.Id` — indices shift when values are added or removed, ids never do.
`Apply`/`Revert` write `AutotileRules` / `TilesetKey` / `TileSize` and publish
`NotifyChanged<TileGridComponent>`, which IS the debounced bake's trigger, so the painted world re-skins
within the bake's quiet window and Ctrl+Z walks a rules edit back like any other scene edit. A rules edit
keeps the tileset and a tileset re-bind keeps the rules (masks are sheet-agnostic; the cell indices are
the designer's to fix up next), and a case can never be emptied — removing its last assignment restores
sheet cell 0,0, which is what `TileGridBaking.PickTile` assumes. Creating a rule set is the SAME
`AddPaintValueCommand` the paint shelf's `+ New` card fires (a rule set IS a paintable index), so the
workspace adds **no parallel data model**: everything it authors is `core.TileGrid` component state that
round-trips byte-stably. The view **heals its binding** every frame — a dead layer or an undone value
re-binds to the first surviving rule set — because undo/redo and deletes can invalidate the selection
under an open workspace.

**Why:** rules authoring needs three panes at once (rule sets, the 16 exposure cases, the sheet); that is
a workspace, not a floating modal over the shell, and Blender's answer to "a different task wants a
different whole-window layout" is a workspace tab. Making the edits live commands rather than a
Save/Cancel buffer is the call the rest of the editor already made — the history IS the safety net (the
one-data-model tenet) — and the designer watches the terrain re-skin while they toggle instead of after
they commit. Refusing entry while Playing keeps the editing-tools-are-inert-while-Playing contract
intact, and deriving `IsOpen` from `ActiveWorkspace` keeps a second, desyncable "is the rules view open"
flag from ever being born.
**Breaks:** a Save/Cancel buffer over the same values re-introduces exactly the parallel representation
the camera block cost three days of bugs; an edit that forgets `NotifyChanged` leaves the world showing
the OLD art until some unrelated change happens to re-bake (the designer concludes the rule "did
nothing"); a workspace that owns the pointer over the top bar traps the designer inside it (no tab, no

content.content: 5	> **Status: Wave A complete (Waves 1–5) + post-Wave-A editor usability + the transport model.** Wave 1 shipped the run-state model (in `foundation`) and the docs that codify it. Wave 2 added the **native scene format** + the **component-serializer registry** (under `Serialization/`) and an additive `AssetKey` on `SpriteInfoComponent`. Wave 3 added the **scene round-trip** (`SceneObjectComponent`, `SceneWriter`, `LoadSceneRequest` + `SceneReaderSystem`, `IPlatformServices.ExportScene`). Wave 4a added the **interactive-editor substrate**: the reference editor composition (in `MonoDreams.Examples.Core`) of the gated game pipeline + editor systems in one world with an in-place `RunMode` flip; `SelectedComponent` + `EditorIdComponent` + `SelectionSystem` (click-to-pick the frontmost sprite); the `EditorHistory` bounded undo/redo with drag-coalescing + the `IEditorCommand` abstraction and the create/delete/transform commands; and `EditorCommandSystem`. Wave 4b added the **transform gizmo** (`GizmoSystem` + `GizmoStateComponent` / `GizmoOverlayComponent` + the pure `Transform/GizmoTransform` math — move/rotate/scale handles, a selection outline, grid-snap, a drag coalesced into one undo step) and the **engine-native toolbar** (`ToolbarSystem` + `Component/ToolbarButtonComponent` + `UI/EditorToolbarBuilder` — tool-select/Save/Load/Undo/Redo/snap on the HUD target). Wave 5 added the **headless editor-op channel** (`Channel/EditorOpPlan` + `Channel/EditorOpReplaySystem`) plus the `CursorInputSystem.SkipHardwareRead` seam, so the real editor systems run headless with no real mouse. **Post-Wave-A usability** added **editor camera navigation** (`CameraNavSystem` + the pure `Navigation/CameraNav` math — middle-mouse pan, scroll-wheel zoom, and a frame-scene key that centres + zoom-fits the camera on all content so off-origin levels are reachable). **Wave 6** extracted the whole editor block into the reusable **composition seam** (under `Composition/`): the `EditorPipelineRegistrar` (named, gate-wrapped, runtime-toggleable pipeline entries — the systems panel's binding surface), the `EditorOverlay` (registry/serializer/history + every editor system + the toolbar + the headless channel, built over the screen's own world), and the `EditorRunFlag` (`--editor` / `MONODREAMS_EDITOR=1` — the screens compose the overlay and the transport boots Paused). **Wave 7** added the **Blender-style editor shell**: in Edit the game composite renders into a smaller centered viewport (`ViewportManager.SetViewportInset` — compositing and mouse mapping follow the same rect) with the chrome placed *around* it at **native window resolution** (`RenderTargetID.Editor` + `EditorChromeRenderSystem` + `RenderLayer.Native`): opaque dark panels (top toolbar bar, right panel strip reserved for the Wave-8 systems panel, bottom strip — `UI/EditorChromeLayout` + `UI/EditorChromeBuilder`) and the toolbar rebuilt in real pixels (hit-testing raw `ScreenPosition`), all kept applied by `EditorShellSystem` (which also makes the OS cursor the one visible pointer). The old HUD-virtual toolbar builder is retired. **Wave 8a** made the overlay **universal** (under the run flag every Examples screen composes it — the menu and the infinite runner included; the overlay can supply its own cursor pipeline to a cursor-less screen via `provideCursorPipeline`), made selection + the gizmo **target-aware** (UI/HUD-target sprites hit-test/drag in virtual space via `VirtualPosition`; across targets the composite order wins — UI/HUD above Main; the entity's own space selects the overlay projection), and shipped the **systems panel** (`System/SystemsPanelSystem` + the pure `UI/SystemsPanelLayout`) in the shell's right strip: every registrar entry of both pipelines, in order, as name + policy tag + live enabled checkbox, toggled through `EditorPipelineRegistrar.SetEnabled`. **Wave 8b** added the **collider gizmo proxies**: colliders are component-local spatial data (not entities), so `System/ProxySyncSystem` materializes standalone proxy entities (`GizmoProxyComponent` bindings under `Component/`, geometry under `Proxy/ProxyGeometry`) over the selected entity's collider shapes; they join the same selection pick (border-only hit-test) and the same gizmo drag (move tool), writing back into the bound component through `Undo/ColliderEditCommand` (one undo step per drag; convex writes refresh `WorldVertices`/`BroadPhaseAABB`). **Post-Wave-8b host wiring** extended the universal overlay **across hosts**: the Demos host (the launcher menu + all four module demo screens) composes it under the same run flag, pairing the overlay with the engine's new `DefaultEditorKeys` default keyboard surface (for hosts without their own action mapping) — the step-by-step recipe any new host/screen follows is [Adding the editor to a screen/host](#adding-the-editor-to-a-screenhost) below. The **transport model** (post-hands-on user directives) retired the F1 mode toggle and the menu's per-level "Edit" buttons / `LevelEditorScreen`: the run flag is the ONLY door, the shell is always visible under it, and `Composition/EditorTransport` owns `RunMode` through the toolbar's left-most **Play/Pause** (one label-swapping toggle button) + **Restart** buttons and the headless `Play`/`Pause`/`Restart` ops — Restart rebuilds the scene from the screen-recorded original load request (history cleared, world-level level components removed, scene entities disposed with `EditorInfrastructureComponent`-tagged/cursor/`KeepAlive` entities surviving; unsaved edits discarded; lands Paused). The **native-resolution overlays + HiDPI wave** (post-transport user directive: “the editor should be rendered at the native screen resolution … like Flutter … gizmos and entity boundaries too”) moved every editor overlay VISUAL (gizmo handles, selection outline, proxy outlines) off the virtual-resolution Main target onto the Editor layer — screen-baked each frame by the draw-side `editor.overlayPrep` pass (`System/EditorOverlayPrepSystem` → `GizmoSystem.EmitOverlays`/`ProxySyncSystem.EmitOverlays`) through the pure `Transform/OverlayProjection` + `Transform/OverlayMeshClip` — and made the whole editor device-pixel aware: on macOS Retina `Composition/EditorHiDpi` re-backs the window at device resolution under the run flag (stock DesktopGL is logical-size + OS-upscaled), `ViewportManager.DevicePixelRatio` carries the ratio, `CursorInputSystem` scales `ScreenPosition` into backbuffer pixels, and the chrome layouts/fonts multiply their point metrics by it. **Island-authoring Slice 1** (the game-anchored phase — see `docs/level-editor/island-authoring-plan.md`) added the **asset palette + placement loop**: an `Assets/` catalog of a gitignored drop folder (`AssetCatalog.Scan` — one entry per PNG plus `*.slices.json` sidecar regions; scan never opens a PNG), runtime `file:` AssetKeys loaded lazily through `Assets/FileAssetTextureLoader` (missing file = loud warning + a visible magenta placeholder, never invisible; `SceneReaderSystem` rehydrates `file:` keys through it), the generic `Assets/SpritePropFactory` (standard prop stack from a catalog entry + a screen-supplied `Assets/PaletteBand`; feet-origin on Y-sorted bands), the coarse **tool modality** `EditorToolMode` on the shared `GizmoStateComponent` (`SelectTransform`/`Place`; selection + gizmo early-out outside `SelectTransform`), the bottom-strip **palette chrome + ghost + click-place** (`System/PalettePlacementSystem` + the pure `UI/PaletteLayout`; placement = one `CreateEntityCommand` undo step, auto-selected; Escape/right-click disarm; headless `palette:<id>` / `band:<name>` ops via the overlay's named dispatch), and the **save guard** (Save is blocked, loudly, while the transport is Playing). **Island-authoring Slice 2** added **order and shape**: within-band ordering (toolbar Bring forward / Send back, headless `order:forward`/`order:back`, PageUp/PageDown on `DefaultEditorKeys` — `EditorCommandSystem` nudges the SOURCE sort fields by `OrderStep`, clamped inside the band via the new `DrawLayerMap.TryGetBandRange`; a Y-sorted band nudges `YSortDepthBias`, never `LayerDepth`, through one `Undo/SpriteSortEditCommand` per click), the **proxy `(kind, index)` generalization** (`ProxySyncSystem` keys its family by kind + element index; per-vertex `ProxyBindingKind.ConvexVertex` handles materialize while the convex family's proxy is selected, and a vertex drag writes back exactly one model vertex — non-convex results rejected loudly, see the premise), **box collider resize handles** (eight edge/corner handles on the box proxy, pure `Proxy/BoxResize` math, one-drag-one-undo through `ColliderEditCommand`), and the **collider authoring actions** (toolbar +Box/+Poly/-Col/+Vtx, headless `collider:*` — footprint default = full sprite width x bottom quarter, feet-anchored, pure `Proxy/ColliderDefaults`; add/remove through the snapshotting `Undo/ColliderComponentCommand`; Delete retargets on proxies: a vertex proxy deletes its vertex with the >= 3 guard, a shape proxy removes its bound collider). **Island-authoring Slice 3** added **walk the island**: the freeform **boundary tool** (`EditorToolMode.Boundary` + `System/BoundaryToolSystem` — click-lay a polyline with a live preview, Enter/double-click commits as one undo step into a `Component/BoundaryComponent{Points,Thickness}` authoring entity, Escape/right-click cancels; per-vertex editing via the reused `(kind,index)` proxy family, `ProxyBindingKind.BoundaryVertex`, on plain selection), the message-driven **`System/BoundaryBakeSystem`** (reacts to the boundary component added/changed → one thin **passive** convex quad segment collider per polyline edge as `ChildOf` `Component/BakedProductComponent` children — static world geometry that blocks; the pure math is `Boundary/BoundaryGeometry`; **bake products are never serialized** — `SceneWriter` excludes them even inside the tagged root's `ChildOf` closure — and re-bake on load/edit, in both run modes), the **trigger palette** (screen-supplied `Assets/TriggerType`s in a palette "Triggers section"; placing one drops a `Passive` box + an auto-numbered `EntityInfoComponent` identity via `Assets/TriggerFactory`; `System/TriggerOverlaySystem` draws the Edit-only tinted outlines + placement ghost; headless `boundary:begin|commit|cancel` and `trigger:<prefix>` ops), and the **walkable-island milestone** verified end-to-end (`IslandMilestoneTests`: build → save → reload → Play walk blocked by coast + footprint, triggers fire with the right identity → Restart rebuilds). The **colliders-as-entities phase (CE-A–CE-D)** then turned a collider into a first-class ENTITY (a shape + its own `TransformComponent`, `ChildOf` a body; box = centered `Size`, no offset) and retired the Wave-8b whole-shape proxy layer: a collider is border-picked and moved/scaled by the ordinary gizmo, **Add Collider ▸ Box/Polygon** creates a child collider entity, `−Col` deletes it, and only convex vertex grips remain proxies — see [`docs/level-editor/colliders-as-entities.md`](../../../docs/level-editor/colliders-as-entities.md). Anything not yet built is marked **(planned, Wave N)**.

feet-origin on Y-sorted bands), the coarse **tool modality** `EditorToolMode` on the shared `GizmoStateComponent` (`SelectTransform`/`Place`; selection + gizmo early-out outside `SelectTransform`), the bottom-strip **palette chrome + ghost + click-place** (`System/PalettePlacementSystem` + the pure `UI/PaletteLayout`; placement = one `CreateEntityCommand` undo step, auto-selected; Escape/right-click disarm; headless `palette:<id>` / `band:<name>` ops via the overlay's named dispatch), and the **save guard** (Save is blocked, loudly, while the transport is Playing). **Island-authoring Slice 2** added **order and shape**: within-band ordering (toolbar Bring forward / Send back, headless `order:forward`/`order:back`, PageUp/PageDown on `DefaultEditorKeys` — `EditorCommandSystem` nudges the SOURCE sort fields by `OrderStep`, clamped inside the band via the new `DrawLayerMap.TryGetBandRange`; add/remove through the snapshotting `Undo/ColliderComponentCommand`; Delete retargets on proxies: a vertex proxy deletes its vertex with the >= 3 guard, a shape proxy removes its bound collider). **Island-authoring Slice 3** added **walk the island**: the freeform **boundary tool** (`EditorToolMode.Boundary` + `System/BoundaryToolSystem` — click-lay a polyline with a live preview, Enter/double-click commits as one undo step into a `Component/BoundaryComponent{Points,Thickness}` authoring entity, Escape/right-click cancels; the pure math is `Boundary/BoundaryGeometry`; **bake products are never serialized** — `SceneWriter` excludes them even inside the tagged root's `ChildOf` closure — and re-bake on load/edit, in both run modes), the **trigger palette** (screen-supplied `Assets/TriggerType`s in a palette "Triggers section"; placing one drops a `Passive` box + an auto-numbered `EntityInfoComponent` identity via `Assets/TriggerFactory`; `System/TriggerOverlaySystem` draws the Edit-only tinted outlines + placement ghost; headless `boundary:begin|commit|cancel` and `trigger:<prefix>` ops), and the **walkable-island milestone** verified end-to-end (`IslandMilestoneTests`: build → save → reload → Play walk blocked by coast + footprint, triggers fire with the right identity → Restart rebuilds). The **native-resolution overlays + HiDPI wave** (post-transport user directive: “the editor should be rendered at the native screen resolution … like Flutter … gizmos and entity boundaries too”) moved every editor overlay VISUAL (gizmo handles, selection outline, proxy outlines) off the virtual-resolution Main target onto the Editor layer — screen-baked each frame by the draw-side `editor.overlayPrep` pass (`System/EditorOverlayPrepSystem` → `GizmoSystem.EmitOverlays`/`ProxySyncSystem.EmitOverlays`) through the pure `Transform/OverlayProjection` + `Transform/OverlayMeshClip` — and made the whole editor device-pixel aware: on macOS Retina `Composition/EditorHiDpi` re-backs the window at device resolution under the run flag (stock DesktopGL is logical-size + OS-upscaled), `ViewportManager.DevicePixelRatio` carries the ratio, `CursorInputSystem` scales `ScreenPosition` into backbuffer pixels, and the chrome layouts/fonts multiply their point metrics by it. **Island-authoring Slice 1** (the game-anchored phase — see `docs/level-editor/island-authoring-plan.md`) added the **asset palette + placement loop**: an `Assets/` catalog of a gitignored drop folder (`AssetCatalog.Scan` — one entry per PNG plus `*.slices.json` sidecar regions; scan never opens a PNG), runtime `file:` AssetKeys loaded lazily through `Assets/FileAssetTextureLoader` (missing file = loud warning + a visible magenta placeholder, never invisible; `SceneReaderSystem` rehydrates `file:` keys through it), the generic `Assets/SpritePropFactory` (standard prop stack from a catalog entry + a screen-supplied `Assets/PaletteBand`; feet-origin on Y-sorted bands), the coarse **tool modality** `EditorToolMode` on the shared `GizmoStateComponent` (`SelectTransform`/`Place`; selection + gizmo early-out outside `SelectTransform`), the bottom-strip **palette chrome + ghost + click-place** (`System/PalettePlacementSystem` + the pure `UI/PaletteLayout`; placement = one `CreateEntityCommand` undo step, auto-selected; Escape/right-click disarm; headless `palette:<id>` / `band:<name>` ops via the overlay's named dispatch), and the **save guard** (Save is blocked, loudly, while the transport is Playing). **Island-authoring Slice 2** added **order and shape**: within-band ordering (toolbar Bring forward / Send back, headless `order:forward`/`order:back`, PageUp/PageDown on `DefaultEditorKeys` — `EditorCommandSystem` nudges the SOURCE sort fields by `OrderStep`, clamped inside the band via the new `DrawLayerMap.TryGetBandRange`; a Y-sorted band nudges `YSortDepthBias`, never `LayerDepth`, through one `Undo/SpriteSortEditCommand` per click), the **proxy `(kind, index)` generalization** (`ProxySyncSystem` keys its family by kind + element index; per-vertex `ProxyBindingKind.ConvexVertex` handles materialize while the convex family's proxy is selected, and a vertex drag writes back exactly one model vertex — non-convex results rejected loudly, see the premise), **box collider resize handles** (eight edge/corner handles on the box proxy, pure `Proxy/BoxResize` math, one-drag-one-undo through `ColliderEditCommand`), and the **collider authoring actions** (the entity context menu's **Collider ▸ Add Box / Add Polygon / Add Vertex / Remove Collider** submenu — the WS wave retired the window-bar +Box/+Poly/-Col/+Vtx text buttons, leaving the menu as the only surface; the headless `collider:*` ops and the dispatch are unchanged — footprint default = full sprite width x bottom quarter, feet-anchored, pure `Proxy/ColliderDefaults`; add/remove through the snapshotting `Undo/ColliderComponentCommand`; Delete retargets on proxies: a vertex proxy deletes its vertex with the >= 3 guard, a shape proxy removes its bound collider). **Island-authoring Slice 3** added **walk the island**: the freeform **boundary tool** (`EditorToolMode.Boundary` + `System/BoundaryToolSystem` — click-lay a polyline with a live preview, Enter/double-click commits as one undo step into a `Component/BoundaryComponent{Points,Thickness}` authoring entity, Escape/right-click cancels; per-vertex editing via the reused `(kind,index)` proxy family, `ProxyBindingKind.BoundaryVertex`, on plain selection), the message-driven **`System/BoundaryBakeSystem`** (reacts to the boundary component added/changed → one thin **passive** convex quad segment collider per polyline edge as `ChildOf` `Component/BakedProductComponent` children — static world geometry that blocks; the pure math is `Boundary/BoundaryGeometry`; **bake products are never serialized** — `SceneWriter` excludes them even inside the tagged root's `ChildOf` closure — and re-bake on load/edit, in both run modes), the **trigger palette** (screen-supplied `Assets/TriggerType`s in a palette "Triggers section"; placing one drops a `Passive` box + an auto-numbered `EntityInfoComponent` identity via `Assets/TriggerFactory`; `System/TriggerOverlaySystem` draws the Edit-only tinted outlines + placement ghost; headless `boundary:begin|commit|cancel` and `trigger:<prefix>` ops), and the **walkable-island milestone** verified end-to-end (`IslandMilestoneTests`: build → save → reload → Play walk blocked by coast + footprint, triggers fire with the right identity → Restart rebuilds). The **colliders-as-entities phase (CE-A–CE-D)** then turned a collider into a first-class ENTITY (a shape + its own `TransformComponent`, `ChildOf` a body; box = centered `Size`, no offset) and retired the Wave-8b whole-shape proxy layer: a collider is border-picked and moved/scaled by the ordinary gizmo, **Add Collider ▸ Box/Polygon** creates a child collider entity, `−Col` deletes it, and only convex vertex grips remain proxies — see [`docs/level-editor/colliders-as-entities.md`](../../../docs/level-editor/colliders-as-entities.md). Anything not yet built is marked **(planned, Wave N)**.

Pressing **Play** runs the game inside the inset viewport with the shell still up; **Restart** rebuilds the scene from the original load (discarding unsaved edits).

Closes #47

Ports the **workspaces + live Autotile Rules editor** wave (WS) from the `roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj` reference into the `level-editor` module, per #47's scope and the three decisions recorded there.

## What shipped

- **Workspaces** — the window top bar gains a Blender-style `[ Level Editor | Autotile Rules ]` tab strip at its LEFT (`WorkspaceTabStripSystem`, 2 hardcoded entries per decision 1), over the new `EditorShellStateComponent.ActiveWorkspace` (`EditorWorkspace` enum; session state, never serialized). The general **Undo / Redo / Refresh** buttons right-anchor beside it (`EditorChromeLayout.TopBarRightRow`). `EditorOverlay.SetActiveWorkspace` is the ONE switch owner: entering Autotile Rules is refused loudly while Playing; editing state (selection, history, active layer, the rules view's binding) survives a switch.
- **The Autotile Rules WORKSPACE** (`AutotileRuleEditorSystem`) — a full-window view: rule-set list (one per `TilePaintValue`, `+ New Rule Set…`), the 16 exposure cases as 3×3 neighborhood glyphs with real-art thumbnails, the bound tileset sheet with `Change Tileset…` (asset-catalog picker), and a **View: DSL** toggle. **Edits are LIVE and undoable** — every tile toggle / tileset pick is one `PaintValueEditCommand` (keyed by the value's stable `Id`) through the ONE shared history; `NotifyChanged<TileGridComponent>` re-bakes the visible world the same frame chain, and Ctrl+Z walks it back. No Save/Cancel.
- **Headless twins** — ops `workspace:level-editor|autotile-rules` and `rules:open|mode|value|case|tile|new|tileset|close`.
- Wired across all 9 editor-composing host screens (`editor.rules` after `editor.contextMenu`; `workspaceTabs` in the `editor.toolbar` group; `RulesEditor.IsOpen` OR'd into keyboard suppression).

## ⚠️ Behavioural change for existing consumers (decision 2)

**`EditorChromeBuilder.DefaultButtons` loses the collider verbs.** The window top bar no longer shows the `+Box` / `+Poly` / `-Col` / `+Vtx` text buttons — the bar is now exactly **Undo / Redo / Refresh**, right-anchored. The verbs moved to the entity context menu's **`Collider ▸`** submenu (**Add Box / Add Polygon / Add Vertex / Remove Collider**): they act on the SELECTION, while the top bar holds app-level verbs. **Nothing was removed — relocated**: the `EditorToolbarAction`s, the `collider:*` ops, and the dispatch are unchanged; the menu paths `collider/add-vertex` and `collider/remove` are new. A Paint-layer selection additionally gets **Edit Autotile Rules…** in its layer block.

## Decision 3 — the full line-read of `AutotileRuleEditorSystem` (944 lines)

The whole file was read line-by-line against the reference during PR preparation. The port is **reference + exactly four adaptations**, all deliberate:

1. **Fixed a latent reference bug**: `TrySheetCellAt` accepted clicks on the sheet pane when *no tileset was bound* (`SheetDims()` falls back to `(1,1)`), so a click on the empty pane pushed a phantom `ToggleTile(0,0)` rules edit onto the shared history. A bound-tileset guard was added; the headless `rules:tile` op calls `ToggleTile` directly and is unaffected.
2. Three `Color.White` → `EditorTheme.NeutralTint` (the module's theme lint blesses only `EditorTheme` roles; the reference is not lint-clean).
3. `WorkspaceTabStripSystem` ported byte-identical.
4. Everything else verbatim.

Audit observations recorded for the record (all inherited from the reference's design, none blocking):
- `ToggleTile` never empties a case — removing the last assignment restores sheet cell (0,0), which `TileGridBaking.PickTile` assumes (now premise-documented + tested).
- The sheet pane pools 200 cell thumbnails — a very tall visible window on a shrunk-cell wide sheet renders its first ~200 cells; scrolling reaches the rest.
- The DSL view renders up to 10 wrapped lines — an extreme alternate count can visually truncate (the canonical string itself is unaffected).
- `HealBinding` re-binds the view every frame, so undo/redo/deletes can never leave it pointing at a dead rule set.
- The Play refusal is **entry-only**: the headless `Play` op can flip RunMode under an already-open workspace (unreachable through the UI — the workspace swallows pointer input below the top bar and the transport buttons sit under its surface). Left as-is to stay faithful to the reference; candidate follow-up.

## Divergences from the reference kept on purpose

Local is ahead of the reference in several files touched by this wave; those local shapes were preserved: no `EditorBottomTab.Paint` (the shelf is ACTIVE-layer-driven since #46), no `createDefaults` on `TileGridPaintSystem`, local `EditorIcons` Eye/EyeOff geometry (the reference's escapes the icon rect), local transport/serializer improvements.

## Tests (all issue items covered)

- **A rule edit re-bakes visibly and undoes** — `AutotileRuleEditorTests.RulesEdit_ReBakesTheTileSourceRects_PerNeighborMask_AndUndoRestoresThem` (the BAKED tile's source rect changes for the edited mask only; undo/redo walk the art back and forth) + 6 more workspace-verb tests.
- **Rule-set CRUD round-trips serialization** — `CreatedAndEditedRuleSet_RoundTripsThroughTheCanonicalSerializer` (create → bind → author → save → load; every undo step round-trips through the FILE) and `RuleSetEdits_AreByteStable_LoadSaveIsAFixedPoint`.
- **Workspace switch preserves both views' state** — `WorkspaceTests` (7 tests: geometry, dispatch, shell-drag suppression, the Playing refusal, the state round trip, chrome parking).
- **Collider verbs reachable via the context menu** — `EditorContextMenuTests` (+6: the four verbs fire the SAME editor commands the retired buttons did; `Edit Autotile Rules…` appears exactly for Paint layers and opens the workspace bound to that layer).

**Gate:** full-solution `dotnet test --configuration Release` green (1275 tests + CLI tests); desktop heads + Demos build clean; `packages.lock.json` untouched.

## Docs

New premise: *"The editor's top-level WORKSPACES are a tab strip at the window top bar's left, and the Autotile Rules workspace edits rule sets LIVE through the ONE shared history"*. Stale text updated in the paint-tab, context-menu, toolbar/chrome, and collider-entity premises + the module overview's status paragraph (the collider-verb relocation and the workspace wave).

#47 (PR #80, 2026-08-07) additions:
- The WS wave landed clean over #46's divergences: kept local's no-`createDefaults` TilePaint ctor, no
  `EditorBottomTab.Paint`, local EditorIcons/transport/serializers (all ahead of the ref). Ported ref bug
  found+fixed: `TrySheetCellAt` accepted clicks on the UNBOUND sheet pane (SheetDims falls back (1,1)) →
  phantom `ToggleTile(0,0)` undo entry; guard added.
- `EditorOverlay` is not unit-constructible (ContentManager/GraphicsDevice/BitmapFont) — overlay-level
  policies (e.g. SetActiveWorkspace's Play refusal) are tested via a documented MIRROR in the test harness
  (the `MenuOver` precedent). If a policy needs real protection, extract a pure static both sites call.
- Play refusal on the rules workspace is ENTRY-only: the headless `Play` op can flip RunMode under an
  already-open workspace (unreachable via UI). Noted in PR #80 as follow-up candidate.
- `EditorThemeLintTests` scans `git ls-files` — `git add -N` new files before running it or the lint
  silently skips them.

description: "How to port waves from the gmtk-2026gj reference repo for issues #45-#57 (the #35 upstreaming batch)"

Issues #45–#57 (the #35 "Upstreaming Witch v Necromancer" batch) port waves from
`roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj` → `Gmtk2026.Core/MonoDreams/<module>/…` (host-screen wiring lives in
`Gmtk2026.Core/Screens/GameplayScreen.cs`). What worked for #48 (PR #71, 2026-08-05):

- Shallow-clone the reference into the scratchpad and **diff file-by-file** against the local
  module — the reference has ALL waves interleaved, so scope by issue: TileGrid/paint = #45/#46,
  workspaces/autotile/collider-menu = #47, layers panel + HUD preview = #48 (done),
  pixel-art asset loop (IHDR auto-grid, .anim cards, file: ladder) = #49 (done, PR #74,
  2026-08-07 — a full local clone already sits at ~/git/roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj, no need to
  re-clone; the in-scope hunks of PalettePlacementSystem/EditorOverlay excluded the Paint-tab
  wave cleanly).
- Some "port items" already landed with earlier issues (the SceneLayer serializer shipped with
  #44) — verify before porting.
- The reference ships NO tests and has latent bugs (its Eye/EyeOff glyph geometry escapes the
  icon rect; MonoDreams' `EditorIconsTests` geometry lint catches it). Author tests fresh from
  the issue's test list; don't trust the reference blindly.
- Two parallel coding agents in one worktree: only ONE may run dotnet (obj/ lock races — see
  [[verify-gate-gotchas]]); the other verifies APIs by reading source. Have both RETURN premises
  text instead of editing premises.md (merge conflicts); the orchestrator integrates.
- Agents' `dotnet restore` can churn `MonoDreams/packages.lock.json` (KNI packages promoted to
  Direct) — revert before committing.
- Sibling-wave PRs collide in the same files (`PalettePlacementSystem`, `premises.md`) — on rebase
  the auto-merge tends to CONVERGE on the reference's shape (it has all waves combined), so verify
  the merged hot spots against the reference file, not against either parent (#50's `StampAt` came
  out byte-identical to the ref after rebasing over #48's layers wave).
- The waves can also break EACH OTHER's lint gates on main: #48's tile-grid merge put
  `TileGridBakeSystem.cs` (raw `Color.White`×5) inside `level-editor`, tripping
  `EditorThemeLintTests` on main itself (found 2026-08-05 while gating #50 — the reference has no
  such lint). Check whether a red gate is pre-existing on origin/main before debugging your branch.

#46 (PR #76, 2026-08-07) additions — divergences #47's rebase will collide with:
- Local DROPPED the ref's write-only `EditorBottomTab.Paint` + `panel:tab paint` op (dead state — the
  paint shelf is ACTIVE-layer-driven), the paint system's unused `createDefaults` ctor param + its
  stale "PaintGrid auto-creation" doc, and `PaintValueEditCommand` (only `AddPaintValueCommand`
  ported into `PaintValueCommands.cs`). Local ADDED the locked-layer loud refusal the ref lacks.
- Ref's `ReflectState` swatch uses lint-illegal `new Color(...)` — the theme lint blesses only
  target-typed `new(...)`; route swatches through a target-typed local.
- Menu-shape tests (`EditorContextMenuTests`) assert exact item counts — adding a menu item is a
  legitimate break; update the facts in the same PR.
- Background `dotnet test ... | tail` masks the exit code (pipe exit wins) — grep the output for
  `Com falha!`/`Aprovado!`, never trust exit 0 through a pipe.

**Why:** the same porting motion repeats for every sibling issue in the batch.
**How to apply:** clone reference → diff → scope by issue number → parallel agents (one builds) →
full Release gate → premises → PR with `Closes #N`.

Done — **PR #80 is open and will close #47 on merge**: https://github.com/roo-oliv/monodreams/pull/80

**What shipped** (one commit, 25 files, +2805/−89):
- **Workspaces**: the Blender-style `[ Level Editor | Autotile Rules ]` tab strip at the top bar's left (`WorkspaceTabStripSystem`, hardcoded-two per decision 1), with Undo/Redo/Refresh right-anchored beside it. `EditorOverlay.SetActiveWorkspace` is the single switch owner — entry refused while Playing, editing state preserved across switches.
- **The Autotile Rules workspace** (`AutotileRuleEditorSystem`): rule-set list, the 16 exposure cases shown visually with a DSL toggle, tileset binding via `Change Tileset…` — every edit a live, undoable `PaintValueEditCommand` that re-bakes the world immediately. Headless `workspace:*`/`rules:*` ops included. Wired into all 9 editor-composing host screens.
- **Decision 2** (flagged prominently in the PR): the collider verbs left the window bar for the context menu's `Collider ▸` submenu; actions, ops, and dispatch unchanged.

**How it went**: one Opus agent ported (build + existing tests green), a second authored 22 new tests (rule-edit-rebakes+undoes, byte-stable serialization round-trip, workspace state preservation, collider verbs via menu) and drafted the premises text, which I integrated into `premises.md`/`overview.md`. The full-solution Release gate passed: 1275 engine + 57 CLI tests, zero failures.

**Decision 3** (the 944-line audit) is recorded in the PR description: the port is the reference plus exactly four adaptations — notably a fix for a latent reference bug where clicking the empty sheet pane pushed a phantom rules edit onto the undo history. One inherited quirk worth knowing: the Play-mode refusal is entry-only, so the headless `Play` op could flip RunMode under an already-open workspace (unreachable through the UI) — noted as a follow-up candidate rather than diverging from the reference.
